resources.string: Your connections, SSH hosts, keys and certificates live only on this phone, sealed by keys that cannot leave it. A backup carries them to another device, protected by a passphrase you choose.
Connections, SSH and database settings, saved queries, CA certificates, and the names and fingerprints of your keys. No passwords, no private keys — on the other device you enter those again.

Everything above, plus the database and SSH passwords and the private keys themselves. Each one has to be unsealed first, so your phone will ask you to authenticate, once per key. Anyone with the file and the passphrase has them all.
The passphrase is not stored anywhere. Lose it and the file cannot be opened — not by us either.
At least %1$d characters. Length is what makes a passphrase hard to guess.
The two passphrases are not the same.
Nothing is written until you have seen what the file contains and said what to do about any connection you already have.
